column2: oracle/acceptance/labelled_questions.tsv -- the labelled question set retrieval is tuned against. Sub-step 3.6.
WHAT THIS IS. A test fixture, not documentation. Every row is a question with an outcome that was
decided BEFORE the threshold was, so that 3.7's confirmation threshold is set by measurement
rather than by feel. Re-tuning a threshold without one of these is guessing.
id       stable. L=lunar, E=economics, X=cross-field, N=negative.
kind     lunar | economics | cross | negative. All three question kinds are covered plus the
negatives, which are what stop a tuner from driving the threshold to zero.
split    tune | holdout. HOLDOUT ROWS WERE NOT LOOKED AT WHILE TUNING. They are scored once,
at the end, against the threshold the tune split chose. A threshold that scores well
on a fixture set its own author also tuned on proves nothing; the holdout is the only
part of this file that can embarrass it.
expect   top       -- target must be the single best (top-ranked confirmed) result
confirmed -- target must appear anywhere in confirmedSet
both      -- every path in target (semicolon-separated) must be in confirmedSet
none      -- confirmedSet must be EMPTY. The corpus does not answer this.
absent    -- target must NOT be in confirmedSet
target   literature/-relative path(s), semicolon-separated. Empty for expect=none.
question the query text, passed verbatim to searchLiterature().
source   where the question came from. Questions inherited from another seat's document are
worth more than questions invented against a filename listing I had just read.
note     what the row is actually testing.
